summary: Long streaming chat hangs mid-response after proxy chunk reassembly failure
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexiDocs reports their long-form streaming chat sessions (SSE) frequently stop emitting further tokens ~30–90s into a multi-minute generation. Client remains connected; no explicit SSE close. This started after 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC deploy of an edge proxy rewrite rule.

Impact:
- Several customers on Dedicated experienced mid-generation stalls affecting production chat features.
- Writes as 'hang' (no new data) requiring user refresh; some users reported multiple attempts to re-request leading to duplicate assistant messages.
- Incident causes downstream timeouts in LexiDocs processing logic; revenue-impacting for high-concurrency workflows during business hours.

Environment:
- Redwood prod, us-east region (edge cluster east-1).
- Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream (SSE) and websocket multiplexing.
- Traffic passes through our new streaming-rewrite proxy that performs HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation and header normalizations for tenant gateways.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided & internal):
1) Create a long prompt that triggers multi-minute generation (e.g., 6k token instruction + large completion target).
2) Start streaming SSE request via curl or browser client.
3) Observe initial token stream for ~20–90s then stream stops sending new data despite model still generating on worker (worker logs show active token production).
4) Client connection remains open; no "event: close" or final bracket is sent.
5) Replaying same request against a bypassed route (skipping streaming-rewrite proxy) completes normally.

Relevant logs / snippets:
- Edge proxy (haproxy-like) shows repeated small writes merged into a bigger TCP segment; upstream chunk boundary markers ("\n\n" SSE delimiter) missing after a particular rewrite path. Example tail: "data: {\"delta\":\"token\"}\r\ndata: {\"delta\":\"token\"}\r\n" then abrupt pause.
- Serving runtime worker logs (timestamps aligned) show generated token batches continuing for another 45s after client-side silence.
- tcpdump on edge indicates a mid-stream rewrite that collapses two chunked frames into one without re-inserting SSE event separators, causing client-side SSE parser to wait for delimiter.
- No 5xx seen; connection not closed by proxy.

Additional context:
- Change rolled out 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC to streaming-rewrite proxy intended to compress headers and reduce TLS handshakes.
- Not every long stream affected; appears correlated with sequences that produce many very small chunk writes (highly tokenized output).
- Customer attempted simple workaround: enable shorter max-token-per-chunk at client side; reduced frequency of stalls but not eliminated.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 Support - Aisha: Logged initial report, asked customer for sample curl + reproducible prompt; requested request IDs and approximate timestamps. SLA P1 acknowledged.
2026-03-10 09:38 Customer - LexiDocs (J. Ramirez): Provided request IDs (req-az3k, req-az3l) and a reproduction prompt; noted that bypassing tenant gateway removes issue.
2026-03-10 11:04 Eng - Diego: Started correlation of proxy logs with worker logs. Noted consistent pattern of chunk boundary loss in rewrite service for affected requests.

2026-03-11 02:46 Eng - Priya Shah: Deployed debug build of streaming-rewrite with additional socket-level write tracing to a canary subset of edge nodes. Observed a specific rewrite code path that coalesces small writes and drops SSE separator insertion under backpressure.

2026-03-12 14:12 Support - Aisha: Communicated interim mitigation to customer: toggle tenant bypass for streaming routes (temporary), ETA for permanent fix provided. Customer enabled bypass and confirmed improved stability.
2026-03-12 18:05 Eng - Diego: Preparing PR to ensure rewrite preserves chunk boundaries and forces flush after each SSE event. Target deploy 2026-03-13 morning UTC.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Proxy byte coalescing removed SSE event delimiters (\n\n) causing client parsers to wait indefinitely for delimiter - supported by tcpdump traces.

Hypothesis 2: HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation routine incorrectly translated 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' boundaries when header compression triggered during rewrite - reproduced locally under high token emission rates.

Instrumented edge rewrite to log raw socket writes and SSE event emission times. Found write batching calls merging two separate event writes into one write without the middle delimiter when backlog > 16KB.
Serving runtime indicates no worker evictions or OOMs during affected sessions; KV cache and model workers continued producing tokens (rules out model-side stall).
Reproduced the failure in staging with same rewrite code and a scripted client that emits many tiny token writes; bypassing rewrite removes the failure.
resolution_notes: Mitigation (short-term): Enabled tenant streaming bypass flag for LexiDocs and other impacted dedicated customers. This routes SSE directly to serving edge without rewrite layer. Customer confirmed immediate improvement.

Fix (long-term): PR merged (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4211) which: a) disables write coalescing for SSE endpoints, b) enforces explicit SSE delimiter preservation during HTTP/2->HTTP/1 translation, c) adds unit tests simulating high-frequency tiny writes.
Deployment plan: Roll out to 5% of edge nodes on 2026-03-13 08:00 UTC, monitor streaming success rate and token delivery latency, then progressive rollout to 100% if metrics stable.

Follow-ups: Add synthetic end-to-end long-stream canary tests to CI (task INT-3882), update runbook with steps to toggle tenant bypass and identify proxy rewrite regressions, and notify customers via status page about 'streaming stability improvement' on 2026-03-14.

Postmortem action items: 1) Add precise SOCK_WRITE tracing for streaming-rewrite, 2) Add alerts for 'stream silence while worker active' pattern, 3) Backport fix to older edge clusters still running legacy rewrite.
